doc.title: John LaPorta interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 13, 1996

title: Teo Macero's 'Fusion' with the New York Philharmonic
summary: In 1957 he and Art Farmer played Macero's 'Fusion' for jazz quintet and orchestra with Bernstein; it was never recorded.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Didn’t you perform with Teo Macero — is that how you pronounce his name?
Didn’t he write a piece that you performed on also?

Yeah. That was in 1957. The piece was called, curiously enough, “Fusion.” And it’s the first use of that word musically that I’m conscious of. And it was a combination of a jazz quintet and Art Farmer was in it, myself, and symphony orchestra. And it was played by, we performed it with the New York Philharmonic with Leonard Bernstein. So it was fairly well received, it’s a shame it was never recorded.
So we played it for a whole week, and that was a great experience.
